description: Keypad Emulation Formats - PIN entry modes (separate from card credentials)
notes: Keypad formats are fundamentally different from card credential formats
Keypad uses BURST MODE - one packet per keystroke
Card formats use SINGLE PACKET with facility + card number
Do not mix keypad formats with card credential formats

keypadFormats.name: 4-bit Keypad (Standard)
keypadFormats.description: Standard 4-bit Wiegand keypad format. Each key press sends 4 bits.
keypadFormats.usage: Most common keypad format. HID, Mercury, Honeywell panels.

keypadFormats.name: 8-bit Keypad (Extended/ASCII)
keypadFormats.description: 8-bit ASCII keypad format. Each key sends ASCII code, # sends Enter (0x0D).
keypadFormats.usage: Extended keypad format. OSDP readers, some HID systems.
notes: # key sends 0x0D (Enter/CR) not 0x23
* key sends 0x1B (Escape) not 0x2A
Digits 0-9 send ASCII codes 0x30-0x39

keypadFormats.name: 8-bit Wiegand Keypad (Farpointe)
keypadFormats.description: Farpointe/legacy 8-bit Wiegand keypad encoding with complement nibbles.
keypadFormats.usage: Farpointe Data readers, some legacy systems.
notes: Each byte is: [high nibble = complement of low nibble][low nibble = key value]
Example: Key 1 = 0xE1 = 1110 0001 (E is complement of 1)

keypadFormats.name: 26-bit PIN (Card Emulation)
keypadFormats.description: PIN sent as 26-bit Wiegand card credential. PIN becomes card number.
keypadFormats.usage: PIN-only mode on card readers. Mercury EP panels.
notes: PIN is encoded as card number in standard W26 format
Facility code is configurable (often 0 or site-specific)
Single packet transmission (not burst)
Used when panel expects card credential but user enters PIN

osdp_KEYPAD.description: OSDP Keypad command - sends keys as ASCII
notes: Real OSDP readers use this command
One key per POLL response in burst mode
Keys are ASCII encoded (0x30-0x39 for digits)
# sends 0x0D (Enter), not 0x23
Used for 26-bit PIN-as-card mode
PIN encoded as Wiegand 26 with facility code
Single packet (not burst)

burst.description: One packet per keystroke, sent on each POLL
burst.termination: # key signals end of PIN entry

single.description: Entire PIN encoded in single packet

mercury.notes: Mercury EP panels support OSDP keypad via osdp_KEYPAD command

hid.notes: HID VertX/Edge typically use 4-bit Wiegand keypad
